title: [Jax][Quantization] compressed-tensors W4A16 linear method on gmm_v2
body:
# Description

Adds a compressed-tensors **W4A16** linear method to the JAX path. Until now `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` raised `NotImplementedError` for every weight-only scheme (`# TODO: w4a8 / wNa16 schemes need their own JAX methods (not yet ported)`). Gemma 4 runs only on the JAX path, so Google's QAT releases (`google/gemma-4-{E2B,E4B,12B,31B}-it-qat-w4a16-ct`) could not be served on TPU. With this PR, 31B serves on a single v6e chip.

FIXES: #3540

**What it supports:** symmetric int4 weights, `group` or `channel` strategy, `pack-quantized` format, no activation quantization. Asymmetric, 8-bit, `actorder=group` and other formats still raise `NotImplementedError` with a specific message.

**Implementation** (`tpu_inference/layers/jax/quantization/wna16.py`):

- `weight_packed`, `weight_scale` and `weight_shape` load onto the host.
  - There they are unpacked with the existing `u32_unpack_i4` (nibbles biased by +8, lowest first) into int4 `[in, out]`, so HBM holds half a byte per weight.
  - `weight_shape` is checked against the layer's dimensions.
  - The merged variant (gate_up) buffers the per-projection shards before unpacking.
- Groups narrower than the MXU run through `gmm_v2` with a `[in // group, 1, out]` scale.
  - The kernel dequantizes each tile in VMEM and multiplies with the unquantized activation, so the full-precision weight never exists in HBM.
  - The cutoff is `gmm_v2`'s own test (`group < mxu_column_size`) evaluated on the attached chip, so a group-128 checkpoint on v5e never takes the kernel's dequantize-after-matmul branch.
- Wider groups, channelwise included, use `xla_quantized_matmul` with a 2D scale. They raise a clear error on a layer whose input dim is sharded, because a `[1, out]` scale cannot be split across the mesh.
- `unpack_wna16_linear_weight` rejects packed words that arrive as a float dtype: a float32 round trip rounds any word above 2^24.

**MoE:** a compressed-tensors MoE scheme other than fp8 now raises at load. Before, it fell back to `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, which read packed int4 experts as dense weights; `cyankiwi/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-AWQ-4bit`, for example, packs its experts as int4. This covers the compressed-tensors case of #3542. fp8 MoE is unchanged: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic` still serves.

**Shortcomings:**

- **Tensor parallelism above 1 is untested.** Every run below uses one chip. The scale sharding, merged-shard reordering and kernel-under-`shard_map` paths follow the existing fp8 and unquantized methods, but are not exercised at TP>1.
- **Small matrices.** The kernel has a fixed cost of about 40 µs per call, so the smallest projections run faster in bf16 (table below).
- **Startup compile is about 2.7x longer than on the XLA path.** 31B takes about 27 minutes cold, and 9 minutes once vLLM's JAX compile cache (`VLLM_XLA_CACHE_PATH`) is kept on disk.
- **Only v6e is measured.** v5e takes the same code paths but is untested.

**Related:** E2B and E4B QAT exports also need #3299 (their KV-shared layers ship no K/V weights). 12B ships as `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`; serve it with `--hf_overrides '{"architectures": ["Gemma4ForCausalLM"]}'`. #2147 and #3487 add W4A16 to the torch path.

# Tests

**Unit tests:** `tests/layers/jax/quantization/test_wna16.py` (18 test cases). They cover:

- dispatch;
- load → process → forward for plain and merged layers, group and channel, against `x @ dequant(W).T`;
- the kernel cutoff at MXU widths 128 and 256;
- rejection of channelwise weights on a sharded input;
- the MoE guard.

They pass together with `test_compressed_tensors.py` on one v6e chip:

```
python3 -m pytest -q tests/layers/jax/quantization/test_wna16.py tests/layers/jax/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py
```

**Decode against real tensors.** 31B layers 0, 5 and 59 were decoded and compared with the same QAT weights in half precision (`google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized`).

| check | result |
|---|---|
| relative Frobenius error | 0.0667 on every projection (int4 quantization error of this export) |
| matmul vs exact dequantize-then-matmul | 0.0022 |

**Per-layer timing, one v6e chip, 16 tokens.** Calls are pipelined, so the numbers are device time.

| projection | bf16 | `xla_quantized_matmul` (2D scale) | `gmm_v2` (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 31B gate_up 5376→43008 | 418 µs | 1654 µs | 168 µs |
| 12B down 15360→3840 | 82 µs | 422 µs | 59 µs |
| E4B down 10240→2560 | 46 µs | 192 µs | 48 µs |
| 31B o_proj 8192→5376 | 30 µs | 298 µs | 43 µs |

Across 24 shape × token cases, the kernel matches the XLA path to 2.4e-3 relative error with no non-finite outputs.

**Serving.** Setup: one v6e chip, `vllm/vllm-tpu@sha256:19a1a0526476f902eb83e1057f3d8938f35b457dd7716a30e9ab4f7bee90d507` (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev468`), `--max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 16`. Throughput is 16 concurrent requests of exactly 256 output tokens (`ignore_eos`), median of 3 passes.

| model | HBM used | output tok/s | vs bf16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| E2B QAT W4A16 | 7.17 GiB | 4060 | 1.14x |
| E4B QAT W4A16 | 10.15 GiB | 2157 | 1.21x |
| 12B QAT W4A16 | 9.46 GiB | 984 | 1.41x |
| 31B QAT W4A16 | 21.67 GiB | 500 | bf16 does not fit one chip |

**Accuracy.** A label read on the 3,880-record public suite, compared per record with the bf16 checkpoint served on the same image:

| model | bf16 | W4A16 | difference (95% bootstrap range) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| E2B | 68.5% | 65.7% | −2.8 pts (−4.0 to −1.6) |
| E4B | 73.1% | 71.4% | −1.6 pts (−2.5 to −0.9) |
| 12B | 76.0% | 75.0% | −1.0 pts (−1.7 to −0.3) |
| 31B | — | 77.6% | — |
